text:
sasha: quick heads-up — ran the fused-FlashAttention variant with fused-RoPE enabled + rotary-dim scaling tweaks on the 1B model workloads this morning. seeing odd p99 regressions when KV cache hit rate > 80% :thinking_face:

ben: can you paste the run config? were you on paged attention or the in-memory path?

sasha: paged-attn path. config: `--attention=flash-fused --rope=fused --rotary-scale=0.75 --kv-policy=prefix-cache --batcher=dynamic-64`

maria: perf-bot posted a summary to prometheus, but quick numbers i pulled: throughput steady, avg latency +3%, p99 +12% for long context (>8k). memory looks fine.

perf-bot: alert: regression detected on eng-ml/flash-fused-rope, job=bench-longctx, p99_latency increased from 42ms -> 47ms (+11.9%), cpu/gpu utilization unchanged.

kyung: interesting. does the regression correlate with sequence length or with the number of kv chunks served from disk?

sasha: correlates with seq len and when prefix-cache yields >80% hits — seems like fused RoPE path triggers an extra copy in the paged kernel when rotary-dim != full-dim. i see extra cudaMemcpy in nvprof output.

ben: can you drop the nvprof snippet? maybe the memcpy is due to alignment fallback when rotary dims are nonstandard.

sasha: nvprof excerpt:
```
GPU memcpy HtoD  1.2ms  (aligned)
kernel: flash_fused_attn_paginated  10.8ms
memcpy DtoD  1.6ms  (kv page evict)
kernel: fused_rope_apply  2.4ms
kernel: flash_fused_attn_paginated  11.2ms
```
(notice the repeated flash kernel runs for the same request path)

maria: that repeated kernel run smells like the fused-rope applied after batching split. are we splitting batches by rotary-dim groups at runtime?

sasha: currently batching heuristic groups by seq length and hardware affinity only. we don't separate by rotary-dim or rope-scale. if fused-RoPE requires a different kernel variant per rotary-scale, runtime decides per-request and may force batch flushes — causing extra kernel boundaries.

kyung: oh — so when a batch includes both scale=1.0 and scale=0.75, runtime flushes and re-dispatches, doubling calls. Solution options: 1) normalize rotary params at request admission (costly); 2) add a fast-path kernel that accepts mixed rotary scaling with runtime branch; 3) relax batching so requests with mixed rotary live in separate batches by default.

ben: +1 for option 2 if we can keep it branchless and cheap. option 3 might reduce effective batch sizes and kill throughput.

maria: we should quantify tradeoffs. i propose a small experiment: run three configs across same load profile (longctx synthetic): A) current runtime grouping (mixed allowed), B) grouping by rotary-scale (strict groups), C) a patched kernel that applies fused-RoPE in a single pass for mixed scales (branching fallback). measure p50/p90/p99, throughput, and extra memcpy counts.

sasha: will run A/B/C in parallel on g4x2. quick results coming in ~2h. tagging @perf-bot to aggregate logs. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

perf-bot: started experiment: exp_id=ef-2026-03-17-fusedrope, groups=[A,B,C], workload=bench-longctx-1B, duration=30m each. logs->gs://redwood-perf/ef-2026-03-17/

ben: also add a microbenchmark for `rotary_scale`=0.5,0.75,1.0 with single-request latency to see knee points. small batch sizes (1-8) matter a lot for PLG traffic.

kyung: note: if we go to mixed-scale fast-path kernel, we must validate numerical parity w/ slow-path (unit tests + nans). fused-rope math interacts w/ quantized kernels differently: low-bit q kernels might need special scaling compensation.

sasha: good call. i'll include parity checks and the quantized 4-bit test. if option C shows <2% p99 uplift vs B while keeping throughput, we can ship that as a immediate mitigation.

maria: thanks. if experiment shows option B wins (strict grouping), we may need to change admission/batcher to include rotary metadata as a grouping key and surface new telemetry so Console can show when grouping is causing flushes.

ben: one more ask — please capture a flamegraph of kernel boundaries in the run so we can see where the extra kernel call happens (shadow traces from batcher).

sasha: will attach nvprof + trace + quick summary when done. ping me if you want to run additional rotary-dim values. :rocket:
